source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

28119.t:
Quitman County backed Colom over Hyde-Smith in the U.S. Senate race by 51 points, 1,654 to 523, with 99% of the expected vote counted. Harris carried it by 31 points in 2024, so the county moved 21 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than the typical Mississippi county's 19-point shift and ranks 34th of 82; every county in the state moved left. The statewide race, at D+0.3, has not been called.

Turnout was 2,205 votes, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Wilkinson moved 15 points, Tunica 13, and Sharkey did not move.

28075.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Lauderdale County went to Hyde-Smith, the Republican, but narrowly: 10,892 votes to 10,528 for Colom, the Democrat, a margin of about 2 points. Trump carried it by 21 in 2024, so the county moved 19 points toward the Democrats. That matches the typical Mississippi county and falls a little short of the statewide swing of 23. All 82 counties moved left. Similar counties moved further: Lafayette and Yalobusha shifted 23 points and flipped to Colom, and Forrest moved 28.

About 21,874 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. The statewide race, nearly tied, has not been called.

28123.t:
Scott County moved about 23 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Colom and Hyde-Smith. Trump carried it by 24 points in 2024; with 99% of the expected vote counted, Hyde-Smith leads by about 1 point, 3,943 votes to Colom's 3,830. The shift roughly matches the state's 23-point swing, which has the statewide race at D+0.3 and not yet called, and beats the typical Mississippi county's 19 points and the national typical 14. Similar counties moved a little less: Leake and Walthall about 19 points, Attala 21.

Turnout was 7,903 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

28017.t:
Chickasaw County swung hard toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race, flipping from a Trump county to one that backed Colom over Hyde-Smith, 3,381 to 2,871. That is a Democratic margin of 8 points, after Trump carried it by 14 in 2024, a move of 22 points. It ranks 25th of Mississippi's 82 counties by size of move; every county shifted left, the typical one by 19 points, and 18 flipped. Similar counties moved alike: Grenada by 19, Winston by 22, Panola by 27.

About 6,338 votes were cast, 88% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Statewide the race is essentially even and AP has not called it.

28033.t:
DeSoto County moved further toward the Democrats than any other Mississippi county in the U.S. Senate race. Trump carried it by 24 points in 2024; this time Colom won it over Hyde-Smith by 7, 29,266 votes to 25,128, a shift of 32 points. All 82 counties in the state moved left, the typical one by 19, and the state as a whole moved 24 as Colom narrowly won. DeSoto outpaced comparable counties: Harrison moved 25, Lafayette 23 and Lauderdale 20.

Turnout fell sharply. The 55,730 votes cast were 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the swing came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters staying home.

28127.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Simpson County voted for Hyde-Smith over Colom, 4,905 to 3,307, a Republican margin of 19 points. Trump carried it by 37 in 2024, so the county moved 18 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly less than the typical Mississippi county (19 points) and the state as a whole (23), where Democrats lead by less than a point and the race is not yet called. Simpson ranks 53rd of 82 counties by move. Lawrence, a similar county, moved 17 points. Monroe and Clarke each moved 22.

Simpson cast 8,377 votes, 76% of its 2024 total of 11,094. Because turnout fell that much, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

28129.t:
Smith County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, but by much less than in 2024. Cindy Hyde-Smith won 3,851 votes to Scott Colom's 1,485, a margin of 43 points, down from Donald Trump's 61-point win over Kamala Harris. That is a 17-point move toward the Democrats, slightly smaller than the typical Mississippi county's 19 and larger than the national typical 14. Similar counties moved about as much: Perry 23 points, Stone 19 and Webster 17.

Turnout was 5,466 votes, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Statewide, Colom leads by less than a point and AP has not called the race.

28087.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Colom and Hyde-Smith, Lowndes County swung 24 points toward the Democrats, from an 8-point Trump win in 2024 to a 16-point Democratic lead, 12,211 votes to 8,834. That is the seventh-largest move among Mississippi's 82 counties, all of which moved left, and above the typical state county's 19 points, the statewide 23 and the national typical 14.

Among similar Mississippi counties, Marshall moved 23 points, Copiah 20 and Warren 17. Turnout was 87% of 2024's, with 21,284 votes cast against 24,426, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. The statewide race has not been called.

28049.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Hinds County gave Democrat Colom 63,302 votes to Republican Hyde-Smith's 14,925, a 61-point margin, up from Harris's 46-point lead over Trump in 2024. That is a 15-point move toward the Democrats. Statewide, Colom won by less than a point in a state Trump carried by 23.

Hinds cast more votes than any other Mississippi county, but its move ranked 71st of 82. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 19 points. Similar Democratic counties moved by comparable amounts: Noxubee by 15, Coahoma by 17 and Leflore by 13.

Turnout was 79,224 votes, 91% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

28035.t:
Forrest County swung harder than almost anywhere in Mississippi. In the U.S. Senate race, Colom (D) led Hyde-Smith (R) 12,064 to 9,749, a 10-point Democratic margin, after Trump carried the county by 18 points in 2024. That 28-point move toward the Democrats ranks second among the state's 82 counties, all of which moved left, and is well above the typical Mississippi shift of 19 points and the national typical shift of 14. Comparable counties moved less: Lauderdale 20 points, Madison 18, Winston 22.

Turnout was 22,433 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Statewide, the race is not yet called.

28025.t:
Clay County gave Democrat Scott Colom a 34-point win over Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in the U.S. Senate race, 5,736 votes to 2,808. In 2024 Harris carried it by 10 points, so the county moved 24 points toward the Democrats, the ninth-largest shift among Mississippi's 82 counties. Every county in the state moved left, the typical one by 19 points, and the typical county nationally moved 14.

Turnout reached 95% of the 2024 level, with 8,619 votes cast against 9,057. Among similar counties, Tallahatchie matched Clay's 24-point move, while Jefferson Davis moved 17 and Adams 14. Statewide, Colom leads by less than a point, and AP has not called the race.

Statewide the race was nearly even and had not been called by AP.

About 5,221 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved a bit further: Attala and Scott came within 3 points, and Leake within 4.

Similar Republican counties moved less: Lee 21 points, Monroe 23, Marion 21.

28133.t:

28081.t:

28091.t:

28001.t:
Adams County backed Democrat Colom over Republican Hyde-Smith in the U.S. Senate race by about 28 points, 6,164 votes to 3,434, with 99% of the expected vote counted. The move matches the typical county nationally but trails Mississippi's typical shift of 19 points, ranking 75th of 82 counties in a state where every county moved left. 28067.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Colom and Hyde-Smith, Jones County stayed Republican but by half its 2024 margin. Hyde-Smith won 12,213 votes to Colom's 7,424, a margin of 24 points, after Trump carried the county by 47 over Harris. That is a 23-point move toward the Democrats, matching the statewide shift and well above the typical Mississippi county's 19 points, ranking 12th of 82. Similar counties moved alike: Lamar by 23 points, Rankin by 22, Lincoln by 15.

Only 20,308 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures should hold, though the statewide race remains uncalled.

28163.t:
Yazoo County flipped in Mississippi's U.S. Senate race, giving Democrat Colom a 19-point win over Republican Hyde-Smith, 4,457 votes to 2,998, with 99% of the expected vote counted. In 2024 the county went for Trump by 2 points, so it moved 22 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than the typical Mississippi county's 19-point shift and slightly less than the state's 23-point swing. Colom leads statewide by less than a point, and AP has not called the race.

Yazoo was one of 18 Mississippi counties to go from Trump to the Democrat, alongside similar counties such as Pike, which moved 21 points. About 7,549 people voted, 84% of the 2024 turnout, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

In the U.S. Senate race between Colom and Hyde-Smith, Humphreys County voted 2,640 to 697 for the Democrat, a margin of 58 points. Harris carried it by 42 points in 2024, so the county moved 16 points toward the Democrats. Turnout held steady at 3,382 votes, 98% of the 2024 total, and 98% of the expected vote is counted.

Every one of Mississippi's 82 counties moved left, but Humphreys moved less than most, ranking 66th against a typical shift of 19 points. Similar Democratic counties moved by comparable amounts: Coahoma 17 points, Noxubee 15 and Tunica 13. Statewide the race stands at D+0.3, a 23-point swing from Trump's 2024 margin, and the AP has not called it.

Tishomingo's shift was smaller than the typical county's 19 points, ranking 72nd of 82, and close to the national typical move of 14.
